title: [YouPass Collect] - UK migration reasons in 2007
prompt: The pie charts show the main reasons for migration to and from the UK in 2007. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the primary motivations behind people's decisions to migrate to and from the United Kingdom in 2007.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, having a definite job offer was the predominant reason for migration in both directions. Additionally, formal study was a far more common reason for immigration than emigration, while the reverse was true for those looking for work and those who did not state a reason.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the major work and study-related motivations, definite employment was the leading factor, constituting 30% of immigration and 29% of emigration. In terms of formal study, there was a striking contrast between the two charts, with over a quarter of immigrants citing this reason, compared to a mere 4% of emigrants. Conversely, looking for work accounted for 12% of those moving to the UK, while it represented a significantly higher proportion of 22% for those leaving.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining reasons, accompanying or joining family members made up 15% of immigration and 13% of emigration. Meanwhile, 18% of emigrants did not state their reason for leaving, which was three times higher than the corresponding figure for immigration, at just 6%. Finally, other unspecified reasons accounted for similar proportions in both directions, at 11% and 14% respectively.
